national.title: How to Apply for a Permanent Driving Licence in India (2026)
national.summary: Step-by-step procedure to convert your Learner's Licence into a Permanent Driving Licence. Complete document checklist, official government fees (₹700), and driving test rules.

steps.title: Complete 30-Day Mandatory Waiting Period
steps.description: Wait at least 30 days after your Learner's Licence (LLR) was issued. Make sure your LLR has not expired (valid for 180 days).

steps.title: Submit Form 2 Application on Sarathi Parivahan
steps.description: Visit sarathi.parivahan.gov.in, select your State, and click 'Apply for Driving Licence'. Enter your Learner's Licence number and date of birth to load your details automatically.

steps.title: Select Vehicle Classes & Driving School Certificate
steps.description: Choose the vehicle classes endorsed on your learner permit (e.g. Motorcycle with Gear - MCWG, Light Motor Vehicle - LMV). If you were trained at an accredited driver training institute (ADTC), upload your Form 5B certificate.
steps.calloutText: Under Section 12 of the Motor Vehicles Act, candidates with a Form 5B certificate from an Accredited Driving School skip the practical RTO driving test.

steps.title: Pay Statutory Government Fees Online
steps.description: Pay ₹200 for DL issue, ₹200 for smart card printing, and ₹300 per vehicle class test fee. Total is ₹700 for single class or ₹1,000 for dual class.

steps.title: Book Practical Driving Test Appointment Slot
steps.description: Select your designated RTO or Automated Driving Test Track (ADTT) and pick an available date and time slot. Download and print the Appointment Slip.

steps.title: Appear for the Practical Driving Test at RTO Track
steps.description: Arrive at the RTO test track 30 minutes before your slot with a vehicle corresponding to your application category. For two-wheelers, demonstrate figure-of-eight (8) balancing and sudden stopping. For four-wheelers, pass the H-track reverse parking, parallel parking, and gradient hill restart without rolling backwards.
steps.where: RTO Driving Test Track / ADTT Center
steps.calloutText: The vehicle you bring for the test must have valid physical registration certificate (RC), active insurance policy, and valid Pollution Under Control (PUC) certificate.

steps.title: Test Results and Biometric Data Verification
steps.description: If you pass the test, the testing officer signs your inspection sheet or the automated track sensors submit an instant electronic pass report. Your digital photo and signature are verified.

steps.title: Receive Driving Licence via Speed Post & DigiLocker
steps.description: Your permanent driving licence number is generated within 24-48 hours and available on DigiLocker and mParivahan. The physical chip-based Smart Card licence is printed and dispatched to your residential address via India Post Speed Post.
steps.calloutText: Once your DL number is generated, your digital driving licence in DigiLocker or mParivahan is legally valid across India under CMVR Rule 139.

faqItems.question: When can I apply for a permanent driving licence after getting a learner's licence?
faqItems.answer: You can apply exactly 30 days after the date your learner licence was issued. You have up to 180 days from LL issuance to pass the test.

faqItems.question: What happens if I fail the practical driving test?
faqItems.answer: You can re-appear for a re-test after a 7-day practice period. Log into Sarathi Parivahan, pay ₹300 re-test fee, and book a new slot.

faqItems.question: Can I take the driving test in an automatic transmission car?
faqItems.answer: Yes. You can bring either a manual or automatic vehicle for your test. However, you must arrange the vehicle yourself as RTOs do not provide cars.

faqItems.question: What is the validity period of a permanent driving licence in India?
faqItems.answer: For private vehicles, it is valid for 20 years or until age 40, whichever is earlier. Above age 50, it is renewed every 5 years.

faqItems.question: Can I drive someone else's car for the RTO driving test?
faqItems.answer: Yes. You can use any roadworthy vehicle with a valid RC, insurance, and PUC certificate. The car does not need to be in your name.

faqItems.question: Is a driving school training certificate mandatory for private cars?
faqItems.answer: No. Driving school training is optional for private vehicles. However, holding a Form 5B certificate from an accredited institute exempts you from the RTO test.

faqItems.question: How do I download my digital driving licence on DigiLocker after passing?
faqItems.answer: Open DigiLocker, select Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, and enter your new DL number. The digital copy carries legal parity with the physical card.

faqItems.question: What is the official statutory fee for a permanent driving licence?
faqItems.answer: The statutory fee is ₹200 for licence issue, ₹300 for the driving test, and ₹200 for smart card printing, totaling ₹700.

rejectionReasons.title: Applying Before 30-Day Mandatory Waiting Period
rejectionReasons.description: Attempting to book a permanent DL test slot when less than 30 days have elapsed since the learner licence was approved.
rejectionReasons.solution: Wait until day 31 from the date printed on your Learner Licence Form 3 before scheduling.

rejectionReasons.title: Expired Test Vehicle Documentation
rejectionReasons.description: Bringing a vehicle to the test track with expired third-party insurance or expired PUC certificate leads to immediate test cancellation.
rejectionReasons.solution: Check mParivahan on your phone to verify the vehicle's fitness, insurance, and PUC are active before visiting the track.

rejectionReasons.title: Failure on Automated Sensor Tracks (Touching Yellow Lines)
rejectionReasons.description: Automated sensor tracks register a fail if vehicle tyres cross boundary lines or exceed allowed forward-reverse maneuvers.
rejectionReasons.solution: Practice parallel parking and reverse H-parking beforehand without crossing side curbs.

rejectionReasons.title: Rolling Backward on the Gradient Hill Restart
rejectionReasons.description: Rolling backwards by more than 12 inches when restarting on the steep gradient track triggers automatic sensor failure.
rejectionReasons.solution: Practice handbrake coordination on inclines to ensure the vehicle moves forward smoothly without rolling back.

rejectionReasons.title: Putting Feet Down or Crossing White Lines on the 8-Track
rejectionReasons.description: Putting your feet down on the ground or brushing the boundary sensors on the figure-eight track fails the test.
rejectionReasons.solution: Maintain smooth throttle control and balance at walking speed without touching your feet to the road surface.

rejectionReasons.title: Expired Learner Licence at Time of Practical Test
rejectionReasons.description: If your Learner Licence exceeds its 180-day validity before your test appointment date, you cannot appear for the driving test.
rejectionReasons.solution: Apply for the practical test within 2 to 3 months of getting your LLR. Do not wait until the final weeks before expiry.

GJ.title: How to Get a Permanent Driving Licence in Gujarat (2026)
GJ.summary: Gujarat operates sensor-based Automated Driving Test Tracks across major RTOs including Ahmedabad, Surat, Rajkot, and Vadodara. Learn slot booking rules, sensor track requirements, and verified Gujarat fee schedules.
GJ.verifiedBy: Civic Research Editorial Team - Gujarat Bureau

steps.title: Complete 30-Day Mandatory LLR Waiting Period in Gujarat
steps.description: Wait at least thirty days after your Gujarat Learner Licence issuance date before booking a permanent driving test slot.

steps.title: Book Automated Test Track Slot on Sarathi Portal
steps.description: Log into sarathi.parivahan.gov.in and select Gujarat to book an automated test track appointment. In Gujarat, morning appointment quotas open daily at 10:00 AM IST.
steps.calloutText: High-volume Gujarat RTO slots open daily at 10:00 AM IST and fill within minutes.

steps.title: Pay Gujarat Statutory Fee via Cyber Treasury
steps.description: Pay the statutory driving licence fee of seven hundred rupees for single class or one thousand rupees for dual vehicle classes.
steps.where: Gujarat Cyber Treasury / Sarathi Payment Gateway
steps.calloutText: Fee includes two hundred rupees for licence issue, two hundred rupees for smart card, and three hundred rupees for driving test.

steps.title: Biometric Verification at Gujarat RTO Center
steps.description: Arrive thirty minutes before your booked appointment. Complete biometric fingerprint capture and original document scrutiny at the administrative window.

steps.title: Appear for Sensor-Based Automated Driving Test
steps.description: Navigate the automated sensor track. For two-wheelers, clear the 8-shaped track without placing feet down. For four-wheelers, complete H-track reverse parking and gradient climb.
steps.where: Gujarat RTO Automated Driving Test Track
steps.calloutText: High-definition cameras and ground sensors record driving errors automatically without human manual interference.

steps.title: Receive Driving Licence via Speed Post in Gujarat
steps.description: Upon passing the automated track, your physical Smart Card Driving Licence is dispatched to your registered address via India Post Speed Post.
steps.calloutText: Your digital driving licence becomes visible immediately on DigiLocker and mParivahan once approved by the licensing officer.

faqItems.question: What are the automated test track maneuvers in Gujarat for cars?
faqItems.answer: Gujarat ADTT tracks test parallel parking, reverse S-bend, H-track parking, and gradient hill stop-and-go maneuvers.

faqItems.question: At what time do Gujarat RTO driving test appointment slots open?
faqItems.answer: Driving test appointment slots in Gujarat open daily at 10:00 AM IST on the Sarathi portal.

faqItems.question: What happens if I fail the automated driving test in Gujarat?
faqItems.answer: You can rebook a fresh slot after seven days and pay a re-test fee of three hundred rupees per class.

faqItems.question: Do I need to take my own vehicle for the driving test in Gujarat?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Bring your own registered, insured vehicle with valid PUC certificate matching the applied licence category.
